His popularity is such that some Taiwanese refer to him as “dad,” a local term of endearment for an admired figure. 在台湾社交媒体上，一些用户对黄仁勋可能做出如此缺乏判断力的行为表示难以置信和失望。他常被当作归来的英雄，长期被视为忠诚的爱家男人。他的人气极高，以至于一些台湾人称他为“爸爸”，这是当地对受敬仰人物的亲昵称呼。 In Taiwan, where fears of a potential Chinese invasion loom over public life, online commentators expressed concern about spying, wondering how Ms. Huang gained entry to the self-governing island. 在台湾，对中国可能入侵的担忧笼罩着公共生活，网络评论人士对间谍活动表示担忧，想知道黄乐是如何进入这个自治岛屿的。 Nevertheless, Mr. Huang could soon be returning to Asia. On Sunday, President Trump indicated he still planned to bring Mr. Huang on his upcoming trip to Asia for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, or APEC, forum hosted in China. Xi Jinping, China’s top leader, is hosting the event, where advanced semiconductor technology and artificial intelligence are expected to be a focus. 尽管如此，黄仁勋可能很快返回亚洲。周日，特朗普总统表示，他仍计划带上黄仁勋参加即将到来的亚洲之行，出席在中国主办的亚太经合组织论坛。中国最高领导人习近平将主持此次活动，先进半导体技术和人工智能预计将是会议焦点。 Xinyun Wu和Siyi Zhao对本文有研究贡献。 Adam Satariano 是时报科技记者，常驻伦敦。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 为什么泰国医生“害怕”肯德基
description: MAX KIM2026年11月9日在曼谷哇集拉医院工作的外科医生塔纳·坦提南开展了一项研究，测试一项与肯德基有关的流行医学迷信。 Lauren DeCicca for The New York Times Thanat Tantinam, a colorectal surgeon in Thailand, knows a lot of things from his medical training, like the ins and outs of the human digestive system, or bowel cancer rates. But also: Never eat Kentucky Fried Chicken at work. 泰国结直肠外科医生塔纳·坦提南从他的医学训练中了解到了许多事情，比如人体消化系统的细节，或是肠癌的发病率。但除此以外，还有一条准则：绝对不要在上班时吃肯德基。 Since he was a medical student, around a decade ago, the American fast food franchise has been the subject of an odd superstition among Thai doctors, many of whom believe that eating its chicken at work will lead to intolerably busy shifts. 大约十年前，他还是医学生的时候，这家美国快餐连锁就已经是泰国医生群体中一个离奇迷信的主题。他们中的许多人深信，在工作时吃肯德基会导致班次极其繁忙，令人难以忍受。 “It’s a serious superstition in some hospitals,” said Dr. Thanat, 35. “Your colleagues might be mad if you bring KFC.” “在某些医院里，这是个十分严肃的迷信，”35岁的塔纳说。“如果你带肯德基来，同事可能会跟你急。” He recently tested this theory. Between 2023 and 2024, he and several co-workers at Phatthalung Hospital in southern Thailand, his employer at the time, conducted a randomized control trial of 345 surgical shifts, comparing metrics like case load or estimated blood loss in patients from three groups of surgeons: a group that ate KFC, another that got food from a local brand named Five Star Chicken, and one that ate nothing. 他最近对这一说法进行了测试。2023年至2024年间，他与当时所在医院——泰国南部博他仑医院的几位同事，针对345个外科班次进行了一项随机对照试验。他们将外科医生分为三组：一组吃肯德基，一组吃本土品牌“五星烤鸡”，另一组什么都不吃，随后比较各组患者的病例数和预估失血量等指标。 在泰国许多医院，医生和护士长期以来一直担心，值班时吃肯德基会招致患者数量突然激增。“五星烤鸡”是对标肯德基的泰国品牌。塔纳的研究追踪了三组外科医生：一组吃肯德基，一组吃“五星烤鸡”，另一组什么都不吃。 The study, which was published earlier this year in the Annals of Surgery Open, a medical journal based in Philadelphia, found that eating KFC does not, in fact, lead to more work. But it also left many questions unanswered: Where did the KFC curse come from? And how had it gripped some of the most educated scientific minds in the country, including Dr. Thanat himself? 这项研究于今年早些时候发表在总部位于费城的医学期刊《外科学年鉴开放版》上。研究发现，吃肯德基实际上并不会导致工作量增加。但这也留下了诸多未解之谜：肯德基诅咒究竟从何而来？它又是如何让这个国家最有学养的科学头脑——包括塔纳本人——深信不疑的？ “Yes, I still believe it — maybe 80 percent out of 100,” he said. “If someone brought me KFC at work, I would keep it until past my shift.” “是的，我仍然相信——大概80%吧，”他说。“如果有人在上班时给我带了肯德基，我会一直放到下班后才吃。” Such superstitions abound in Thailand, where Buddhism has blended with a mélange of other spiritual traditions like animism, Hindu rituals and Chinese astrology to create a strong affinity for the supernatural in contemporary life. 这种迷信在泰国极为普遍。在这里，佛教与万物有灵论、印度教仪式及中国占星术等其他精神传统相融合，使得当代生活与超自然现象产生了强烈的联结。 “In Thailand, superstition isn’t the opposite of modernity — it lives comfortably alongside it,” said Theeranuch Pusaksrikit, a business school professor at Chulalongkorn University who researches how superstitions affect consumerist behavior. “The same person can hold a science degree, consult an auspicious date before signing a contract and wear an amulet to work.” “在泰国，迷信并非现代性的对立面，而是与现代性和谐共存，”朱拉隆功大学商学院研究迷信如何影响消费行为的教授提拉努·普萨斯里吉表示。“同一个人可以拥有科学学位，在签合同前查阅黄道吉日，然后戴着护身符去上班。” ‘This Is Not KFC’ “这不是肯德基” No occasion is too big or too small for a sprinkle of superstition. There are the infamous black magic rituals that occasionally surface in politics, and popular customs like dressing in lucky colors corresponding to each day of the week. Last year, when a sinkhole opened up and stranded a pickup truck near Bangkok’s Vajira Hospital, Dr. Thanat’s current employer, people rushed to buy lottery tickets matching the vehicle’s license plate number. 无论场合大小，人们总能掺杂一点迷信元素。有时政领域偶尔浮现的臭名昭著的黑魔法仪式，也有按一周每天的幸运色穿衣的流行习俗。去年，当曼谷哇集拉医院（塔纳目前在那里就职）附近发生地陷并困住一辆皮卡车时，人们纷纷抢购与该车车牌号一致的彩票。 “Each hospital has their own superstition culture,” Dr. Thanat said. He has also heard of colleagues avoiding nuts, pizza or coffee while at work, and knows of at least one hospital where bananas — otherwise regarded as a lucky food — are taboo. “每家医院都有属于自己的迷信文化，”塔纳说。他还听说有同事在上班时不碰坚果、披萨或咖啡，并且知道至少有一家医院将香蕉列为禁忌，尽管它在其他地方常被视为吉祥食物。 曼谷的一名医护人员拿取送到哇集拉医院的椰奶甜点外卖。许多泰国医生和护士将肯德基视为工作时的饮食禁忌。10月，一名护士在曼谷哇集拉医院外购买水果。在泰国，香蕉通常被视为一种吉祥食物。 But few medical superstitions have been as universal and long-running as the KFC curse, a fact that has been a point of fascination at KFC itself. 然而，很少有医学迷信能像“肯德基诅咒”这般普遍且持久，这甚至引起了肯德基自身的极大兴趣。 “We dug into the data, it was pretty clear,” said Suhayl Limbada, who was until recently the chief marketing officer of KFC Thailand. “There was a noticeable trend at restaurants around hospitals, there was a dip in sales.” “我们深入分析了数据，结果非常明显，”前不久还担任肯德基泰国区首席营销官的苏海尔·林巴达说。“医院周边餐厅出现了一个明显的趋势，销售额会下降。” Two years ago, he parlayed the curse into a marketing campaign. Though riffing on cultural practices had gotten Mr. Limbada in trouble before — the fried chicken-scented incense sticks the company released for Lunar New Year were widely panned — this one was much more warmly received. 两年前，他将这一诅咒转化利用为一场营销活动。尽管拿文化习俗做文章曾让林巴达惹上过麻烦——该公司为农历新年推出的炸鸡味线香就曾广受批评，但这次活动受到了欢迎。 Launched on doctor’s day in November 2024, the campaign offered a kind of cleansing ritual: Chicken was sold in packaging labeled with slogans like “This is not KFC” in stores near hospitals. 活动于2024年11月的医生节推出，提供了一种类似净化的仪式：在医院附近的门店里，炸鸡包装上印有“这不是肯德基”之类的标语进行售卖。 直肠外科医生塔纳在他位于哇集拉医院的办公室里。尽管肯德基厄运已被科学证伪，他表示自己依然相信它。塔纳的这项研究于今年早些时候发表在医学期刊《外科学年鉴开放版》上，研究发现，吃肯德基并不会导致工作量增加。 Mr. Limbada has his own ideas about how the curse came to be. KFC opened in Thailand in 1984 and has since become one of the most ubiquitous fast food franchises in the country — and a trailblazer of late night delivery. It operates around 1,300 stores, far outnumbering McDonald’s, which has around 240. In even the smallest rural town, chances are there is at least a KFC. 对于这个诅咒的由来，林巴达有自己的看法。肯德基在1984年进入泰国，此后便成为该国最普及的快餐连锁店之一，同时也是深夜外卖的先驱。它拥有约1300家门店，数量远超约有240家门店的麦当劳。哪怕是在最偏远的乡村小镇，也很可能至少有一家肯德基。 He thinks one of these rural locations might have been the ground zero, delivering one late night to an understaffed local hospital where a hungry doctor, unaware that they were about to be hit with a sanity-shattering deluge of patients, was waiting. 他认为，这些乡村门店中的某一家可能就是诅咒的发源地。在某个深夜，一份外卖被送到当地一家人手短缺的医院，那里有一位饥肠辘辘的医生正在等待，他并不知道自己即将被如潮水般涌来、令人精神崩溃的病患潮所淹没。 Building Solidarity 形成凝聚力 The superstition has since racked up a catalog of very specific lore. 自那时起，这种迷信便衍生出了一系列非常具体的传说。 It is widely understood, for example, that it only applies to departments that cannot easily leave the hospital for meals, like surgery or emergency rooms, said Titaporn Nasaarn, a 34-year-old ER doctor at Kamalasai Hospital in northeastern Thailand. 例如泰国东北部加马拉赛医院34岁的急诊科医生提塔蓬·纳萨安说，大家普遍默认它只适用于像外科或急诊室这样不便离开医院就餐的科室。 She recalled how her colleagues once successfully co-opted the superstition for good. It was during an unusually quiet evening in the surgical intensive care unit, and some of the nurses, who wanted to work, were worried they were going to lose their upcoming shifts. 她回忆起同事们曾有一次成功将这种迷信派上了用场。那是在外科重症监护室一个异常平静的夜晚，一些想干活的护士担心她们会失去接下来的排班。 “The attending anesthesiologist performed a ritual to summon cases by ordering KFC and ordering pizza,” she said. The beds filled up. But “normally, hardly anyone dares to order it,” she added. “值班麻醉师通过点肯德基和披萨进行了一场召唤病例的仪式，”她说。随后病床果然住满了。不过她补充道：“通常情况下，几乎没有人敢去点它。” To everyone else, of course, KFC, with Thai spinoffs like Green Curry Chicken Rice, remains a desirable food. And at many hospitals, patients or their families occasionally treat their medical caretakers to the stuff, a gesture that invariably puts Jaruda Mamuangbon, a 42-year-old nurse at Vajira Hospital, on edge. 当然，对于其他人而言，提供绿咖喱鸡肉饭等泰国本土化产品的肯德基依然是诱人的美食。在许多医院，患者或其家属有时会买这些东西来犒劳医护人员，但这一举动总会让哇集拉医院42岁的护士贾鲁达·马孟本神经紧绷。 在曼谷哇集拉医院，护士贾鲁达·马孟本向一名患者行泰国传统敬意手势“合十礼”。在曼谷哇集拉医院，患者们正在等待配药。许多患者会带来礼物以感谢医护人员。但随着关于该厄运的消息传开，送肯德基作为礼物的情况已经减少。 But she and her colleagues have noticed that the number of KFC gifts has plummeted in the last two or so years. 不过她和同事们已经注意到，在过去大概两年里，收到肯德基礼物的情况已经大幅减少。 “We have always graciously accepted the kind gift,” Ms. Jaruda said. “But I think the patients’ families have probably picked up on the superstition from social media.” “我们一直都礼貌地接受这份心意，”贾鲁达说。“但我认为患者家属可能已经从社交媒体上获知了这种迷信。” Ms. Theeranuch, the professor, sees the widespread belief in the jinx not as a posture of anti-science, but a way for Thailand’s medical workers to keep their spirits up. 提拉努认为，人们对这种厄运的普遍信仰并非反科学，而是泰国医护人员保持精神振奋的一种方式。 “Hospital work is intensely unpredictable, and a shared rule like ‘don’t eat KFC on shift’ may give staff a small sense of control over something inherently unpredictable,” she said. “They also build solidarity.” “医院工作充满了极大的不确定性，在面对那些本质上不可预测的事物时，‘值班时不吃肯德基’这种共同规则或许能让员工获得些许控制感，”她说。“他们还能形成凝聚力。” Dr. Thanat has settled into a similar view. Underneath the supernatural dress of the KFC curse are, he said, more sobering earthbound realities. 塔纳也抱有类似的看法。他表示，在肯德基诅咒那超自然的外表下，隐藏着更令人清醒的现实问题。 It is telling that the curse has largely been confined to the country’s public hospitals, where doctors — overworked and underpaid compared with their private sector counterparts — have long called for better working conditions. 值得注意的是，这种诅咒主要局限于该国的公立医院。那里的医生长期面临工作强度大且薪酬低于私营部门同行的问题，并一直呼吁改善工作条件。 “If you work at a private hospital, you would want more patients to come,” Dr. Thanat said, adding that doctors’ compensation at private hospitals scales with greater caseloads. “如果你在私立医院工作，你会希望有更多患者来看病，”塔纳说，因为私立医院医生的收入是与病例数挂钩的。 “I think the KFC curse is a projection of fear,” he said. “We need a scapegoat.” “我认为肯德基诅咒是恐惧的一种投射，”他说。“我们需要一个替罪羊。” Phuriphat Dejsuphong对本文有报道贡献。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。

There are the infamous black magic rituals that occasionally surface in politics, and popular customs like dressing in lucky colors corresponding to each day of the week. Last year, when a sinkhole opened up and stranded a pickup truck near Bangkok’s Vajira Hospital, Dr. Thanat’s current employer, people rushed to buy lottery tickets matching the vehicle’s license plate number. 无论场合大小，人们总能掺杂一点迷信元素。有时政领域偶尔浮现的臭名昭著的 黑魔法仪式 ，也有按一周每天的幸运色穿衣的流行习俗。去年，当曼谷哇集拉医院（塔纳目前在那里就职）附近发生地陷并困住一辆皮卡车时，人们纷纷抢购与 该车车牌号 一致的彩票。 “Each hospital has their own superstition culture,” Dr. Thanat said. He has also heard of colleagues avoiding nuts, pizza or coffee while at work, and knows of at least one hospital where bananas — otherwise regarded as a lucky food — are taboo. “每家医院都有属于自己的迷信文化，”塔纳说。他还听说有同事在上班时不碰坚果、披萨或咖啡，并且知道至少有一家医院将香蕉列为禁忌，尽管它在其他地方常被视为吉祥食物。 曼谷的一名医护人员拿取送到哇集拉医院的椰奶甜点外卖。许多泰国医生和护士将肯德基视为工作时的饮食禁忌。 10月，一名护士在曼谷哇集拉医院外购买水果。在泰国，香蕉通常被视为一种吉祥食物。 But few medical superstitions have been as universal and long-running as the KFC curse, a fact that has been a point of fascination at KFC itself. 然而，很少有医学迷信能像“肯德基诅咒”这般普遍且持久，这甚至引起了肯德基自身的极大兴趣。 “We dug into the data, it was pretty clear,” said Suhayl Limbada, who was until recently the chief marketing officer of KFC Thailand. “There was a noticeable trend at restaurants around hospitals, there was a dip in sales.” “我们深入分析了数据，结果非常明显，”前不久还担任肯德基泰国区首席营销官的苏海尔·林巴达说。“医院周边餐厅出现了一个明显的趋势，销售额会下降。” Two years ago, he parlayed the curse into a marketing campaign. Though riffing on cultural practices had gotten Mr. Limbada in trouble before — the fried chicken-scented incense sticks the company released for Lunar New Year were widely panned — this one was much more warmly received. 两年前，他将这一诅咒 转化利用 为一场营销活动。尽管拿文化习俗做文章曾让林巴达惹上过麻烦——该公司为农历新年推出的炸鸡味线香就曾广受批评，但这次活动受到了欢迎。 Launched on doctor’s day in November 2024, the campaign offered a kind of cleansing ritual: Chicken was sold in packaging labeled with slogans like “This is not KFC” in stores near hospitals. 活动于2024年11月的医生节推出，提供了一种类似净化的仪式：在医院附近的门店里，炸鸡包装上印有“这不是肯德基”之类的标语进行售卖。 直肠外科医生塔纳在他位于哇集拉医院的办公室里。尽管肯德基厄运已被科学证伪，他表示自己依然相信它。 塔纳的这项研究于今年早些时候发表在医学期刊《外科学年鉴开放版》上，研究发现，吃肯德基并不会导致工作量增加。 Mr. Limbada has his own ideas about how the curse came to be. KFC opened in Thailand in 1984 and has since become one of the most ubiquitous fast food franchises in the country — and a trailblazer of late night delivery. It operates around 1,300 stores, far outnumbering McDonald’s, which has around 240. In even the smallest rural town, chances are there is at least a KFC. 对于这个诅咒的由来，林巴达有自己的看法。肯德基在1984年进入泰国，此后便成为该国最普及的快餐连锁店之一，同时也是深夜外卖的先驱。它拥有约1300家门店，数量远超约有240家门店的麦当劳。哪怕是在最偏远的乡村小镇，也很可能至少有一家肯德基。 He thinks one of these rural locations might have been the ground zero, delivering one late night to an understaffed local hospital where a hungry doctor, unaware that they were about to be hit with a sanity-shattering deluge of patients, was waiting. 他认为，这些乡村门店中的某一家可能就是诅咒的发源地。在某个深夜，一份外卖被送到当地一家人手短缺的医院，那里有一位饥肠辘辘的医生正在等待，他并不知道自己即将被如潮水般涌来、令人精神崩溃的病患潮所淹没。 Building Solidarity 形成凝聚力 The superstition has since racked up a catalog of very specific lore. 自那时起，这种迷信便衍生出了一系列非常具体的传说。 It is widely understood, for example, that it only applies to departments that cannot easily leave the hospital for meals, like surgery or emergency rooms, said Titaporn Nasaarn, a 34-year-old ER doctor at Kamalasai Hospital in northeastern Thailand. 例如泰国东北部加马拉赛医院34岁的急诊科医生提塔蓬·纳萨安说，大家普遍默认它只适用于像外科或急诊室这样不便离开医院就餐的科室。 She recalled how her colleagues once successfully co-opted the superstition for good. It was during an unusually quiet evening in the surgical intensive care unit, and some of the nurses, who wanted to work, were worried they were going to lose their upcoming shifts. 她回忆起同事们曾有一次成功将这种迷信派上了用场。那是在外科重症监护室一个异常平静的夜晚，一些想干活的护士担心她们会失去接下来的排班。 “The attending anesthesiologist performed a ritual to summon cases by ordering KFC and ordering pizza,” she said. The beds filled up. But “normally, hardly anyone dares to order it,” she added. “值班麻醉师通过点肯德基和披萨进行了一场召唤病例的仪式，”她说。随后病床果然住满了。不过她补充道：“通常情况下，几乎没有人敢去点它。” To everyone else, of course, KFC, with Thai spinoffs like Green Curry Chicken Rice, remains a desirable food. And at many hospitals, patients or their families occasionally treat their medical caretakers to the stuff, a gesture that invariably puts Jaruda Mamuangbon, a 42-year-old nurse at Vajira Hospital, on edge. 当然，对于其他人而言，提供绿咖喱鸡肉饭等泰国本土化产品的肯德基依然是诱人的美食。在许多医院，患者或其家属有时会买这些东西来犒劳医护人员，但这一举动总会让哇集拉医院42岁的护士贾鲁达·马孟本神经紧绷。 在曼谷哇集拉医院，护士贾鲁达·马孟本向一名患者行泰国传统敬意手势“合十礼”。 在曼谷哇集拉医院，患者们正在等待配药。许多患者会带来礼物以感谢医护人员。但随着关于该厄运的消息传开，送肯德基作为礼物的情况已经减少。 But she and her colleagues have noticed that the number of KFC gifts has plummeted in the last two or so years. 不过她和同事们已经注意到，在过去大概两年里，收到肯德基礼物的情况已经大幅减少。 “We have always graciously accepted the kind gift,” Ms. Jaruda said. “But I think the patients’ families have probably picked up on the superstition from social media.” “我们一直都礼貌地接受这份心意，”贾鲁达说。“但我认为患者家属可能已经从社交媒体上获知了这种迷信。” Ms. Theeranuch, the professor, sees the widespread belief in the jinx not as a posture of anti-science, but a way for Thailand’s medical workers to keep their spirits up. 提拉努认为，人们对这种厄运的普遍信仰并非反科学，而是泰国医护人员保持精神振奋的一种方式。 “Hospital work is intensely unpredictable, and a shared rule like ‘don’t eat KFC on shift’ may give staff a small sense of control over something inherently unpredictable,” she said. “They also build solidarity.” “医院工作充满了极大的不确定性，在面对那些本质上不可预测的事物时，‘值班时不吃肯德基’这种共同规则或许能让员工获得些许控制感，”她说。“他们还能形成凝聚力。” Dr. Thanat has settled into a similar view. Underneath the supernatural dress of the KFC curse are, he said, more sobering earthbound realities. 塔纳也抱有类似的看法。他表示，在肯德基诅咒那超自然的外表下，隐藏着更令人清醒的现实问题。 It is telling that the curse has largely been confined to the country’s public hospitals, where doctors — overworked and underpaid compared with their private sector counterparts — have long called for better working conditions. 值得注意的是，这种诅咒主要局限于该国的公立医院。那里的医生长期面临工作强度大且薪酬低于私营部门同行的问题，并一直呼吁改善工作条件。 “If you work at a private hospital, you would want more patients to come,” Dr. Thanat said, adding that doctors’ compensation at private hospitals scales with greater caseloads. “如果你在私立医院工作，你会希望有更多患者来看病，”塔纳说，因为私立医院医生的收入是与病例数挂钩的。 “I think the KFC curse is a projection of fear,” he said. “We need a scapegoat.” “我认为肯德基诅咒是恐惧的一种投射，”他说。“我们需要一个替罪羊。” Phuriphat Dejsuphong对本文有报道贡献。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 英伟达先进芯片流向中国“空壳”公司
description: ANA SWANSON, KALLEY HUANG, KEITH BRADSHER2026年11月9日北京的一处高科技企业工业园区。新矩阵公司将该建筑列为其地址，但园区公司名录中并未收录该企业。 The New York Times In a recently built industrial park on the northwest fringe of Beijing, the listed address of a company called New Matrix stands empty, a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be. 在北京西北郊一个最近建成的工业园区里，一家名为新矩阵的公司登记地址空无一人，那是一个空荡荡的灰色房间，天花板上本该装灯的地方垂着电线。 Earlier this year, the Trump administration approved this Chinese firm to assemble Nvidia’s advanced chips into the computers that create artificial intelligence. President Trump allowed the sale of the chips, called the H200, to China late last year. But before they could be sold, the Commerce Department was required to review the companies involved for national security risks. 今年早些时候，特朗普政府批准这家中国公司组装英伟达的先进芯片，用于创建人工智能的计算机。特朗普去年年底允许向中国出售这种名为H200的芯片。但在芯片出售之前，美国商务部必须对相关企业进行审查，以评估其是否存在国家安全风险。 New Matrix passed that review. Yet recent checks by The New York Times found that, within China, there is little evidence the firm actually exists, raising questions about who in China is behind the company. 新矩阵通过了这项审查。然而，《纽约时报》近期的核查发现，在中国国内，几乎没有证据表明这家公司真实存在，这引发了关于究竟是谁在幕后掌控这家公司的疑问。 Only scant information can be found online about New Matrix, which was created 17 months ago. At the building that New Matrix lists as its address, a company directory does not include the firm. At the nearby property management agency for the industrial park, a receptionist and a manager both said they had no record of the company. 关于这家17个月前成立的公司，网上只能找到极少信息。在新矩阵登记地址所在的大楼里，公司名录中没有这家公司。在附近工业园区的物业管理处，一名接待员和一名经理都说没有该公司的记录。 According to Chinese corporate records, New Matrix’s owners have ties to a prominent Chinese private equity fund that the U.S. government placed on a trade blacklist in 2024. Two analysts who examined the corporate records and other Chinese-language information said they believed New Matrix may be a front for firms associated with that fund. 根据中国企业登记记录，新矩阵的所有者与一家知名中国私募股权基金有关联，该基金已于2024年被美国政府列入贸易黑名单。两名审查了公司记录和其他中文信息的分析师表示，他们认为新矩阵可能是与该基金有关公司的幌子。 The sale of chips to New Matrix appears to be part of a pattern that has concerned technology experts inside and outside the government: The Commerce Department is giving clearance to buy and handle Nvidia’s chips to Chinese companies with ties to firms that have been subject to national-security-related trade restrictions. 芯片流向新矩阵似乎是令政府内外技术专家担忧的一种模式的一部分：美国商务部正在批准某些中国公司购买和处理英伟达芯片，而这些公司与此前被列入国家安全相关贸易限制的中国企业有关联。 Nvidia’s chips are the crucial technology in A.I. data centers and now one of the world’s most coveted commodities. They are also at the heart of the economic and geopolitical competition between the United States and China. 英伟达的芯片是人工智能数据中心的关键技术，如今也是世界上最抢手的商品之一。它们也是美中经济与地缘政治竞争的核心。 Corporate records show that several other Chinese companies approved to purchase H200 chips or assemble them into servers have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China. 公司记录显示，其他几家获准购买H200芯片或将其组装成服务器的中国公司与被美国政府列入黑名单的公司有关联，或者在中国担任军事承包商运营。 Liza Tobin, the former China director for the White House National Security Council in the first Trump and Biden administrations, said the approvals raised questions about how rigorously the Trump administration is policing who can get their hands on Nvidia’s chips. 曾在特朗普和拜登政府时期担任白宫国家安全委员会中国事务主任的莉莎·托宾说，这些批准引发了疑问：特朗普政府在监管谁能获得英伟达芯片方面究竟有多严格。 “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” she said. “我有很多担忧，商务部和英伟达都没有进行必要的尽职调查，以确保许可条款得到遵守，”她说。 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋，该公司的芯片是人工智能数据中心的关键技术，如今已成为全球最抢手的商品之一。 During the Biden administration, the United States began more broadly restricting sales of A.I. chips to China out of concern the technology would help China advance militarily. But Mr. Trump eased some of those limits after lobbying by Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, with whom he has grown close during his second term. 在拜登政府时期，美国开始更广泛地限制向中国出售人工智能芯片，担心该技术会帮助中国推进军事发展。但特朗普在英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的游说下放松了部分限制，他在第二任期内与黄仁勋的关系日益密切。 In December, Mr. Trump gave Nvidia permission to sell the H200, an older but still powerful A.I. chip, to China, as long as the U.S. government was given a cut of the sales. 去年12月，特朗普允许英伟达向中国出售H200——一款较旧但仍性能强大的人工智能芯片，条件是美国政府从销售中抽成。 In an unusual arrangement, Mr. Trump is requiring these chips, which are assembled in Taiwan, to be routed through the United States on their way to China, so that the government can collect a 25 percent tariff on their value. 在一项不同寻常的安排中，特朗普要求这些在台湾组装的芯片在运往中国途中经过美国，以便政府对其价值征收25%的关税。 Nvidia is now selling only small amounts of H200 chips to China. The Chinese government has been slow to approve its companies for the purchases, partly because it is trying to promote domestically made chips. 英伟达目前只向中国出售少量H200芯片。中国政府一直缓慢批准本国公司购买，部分原因是它试图推广国产芯片。 Although China is a potentially huge market for A.I. technology, sales directly to the country currently account for only a tiny percentage of Nvidia’s revenue. In the quarter that ended in July, H200 shipments to customers based in China made up less than 1 percent of Nvidia’s revenue from data centers. The company also said in August that it was not assuming any sales to China in its estimate for data center revenue for the current quarter. 尽管中国是人工智能技术的潜在巨大市场，但直接对华销售目前仅占英伟达收入的很小比例。在截至7月的财季中，向位于中国的客户交付H200的出货量不到英伟达数据中心收入的1%。公司还在8月表示，在对本财季度数据中心营收的预估中，并未将对华销售额纳入考量。 But many Chinese companies are gaining access to Nvidia chips through data centers in Southeast Asia, and the chips still appear to be a critical focus for Beijing. The Times reported last month that Mr. Huang of Nvidia had a close relationship with a woman who American spy agencies concluded was an intelligence asset for China. The company she worked at, Megaspeed, operated data centers in Southeast Asia that served Chinese clients and was being investigated for smuggling some chips into China. On Sunday, Nvidia said that it was opening an investigation into Mr. Huang’s relationship with the woman after he acknowledged to the company’s board that he had been intimate with her. 但许多中国企业正通过东南亚的数据中心获得英伟达芯片，而这些芯片似乎仍是北京关注的焦点。《纽约时报》上个月报道，英伟达的黄仁勋与一名女性关系密切，美国间谍机构认定她是中国的情报人员。她所在的公司Megaspeed在东南亚运营数据中心，为中国客户服务，并因涉嫌将一些芯片走私到中国而受到调查。周日，英伟达表示，在黄仁勋向公司董事会承认他与该女性有亲密关系后，公司正在调查黄仁勋与她的关系。 《纽约时报》记者走访时发现，获特朗普政府批准将英伟达的先进芯片组装成人工智能计算机的新矩阵公司登记地址处空无一人。 Another Empty Office 另一个空办公室 When the Commerce Department granted its approval to New Matrix this year, the company’s registered address was at a compound on the outskirts of Beijing used for corporate registrations, where thousands of other firms are also registered on paper, according to the Chinese corporate information site Qichacha. But this fall, New Matrix’s address changed to the empty office in the industrial park visited by The Times. 根据中国公司信息网站企查查，今年美国商务部对新矩阵给与批准之时，该公司的注册地址在北京郊区一个用于公司注册的园区，该园区还有数千家其他公司于名义上在此注册。但今年秋天，新矩阵的地址变更为《纽约时报》探访的工业园区那间空办公室。 New Matrix’s website does not name any staff members, advertise any jobs or include information about its history, as of Nov. 6. But two of its primary owners appear in the records of companies connected to a Chinese private equity firm under sanctions and its founder, a man named Li Bin, according to WireScreen, a data platform. 截至11月6日，新矩阵的网站没有列出任何员工姓名，没有布任何招聘信息，也没有包含关于其历史的信息。但根据数据平台WireScreen，其两名主要所有者出现在一家受制裁的中国私募股权公司及其创始人的关联企业记录中，该创始人名为李斌。 In 2024, the U.S. government added the private equity firm, Wise Road, to the Commerce Department’s “entity list,” which restricts companies from doing business with the United States. The department said Wise Road had helped the Chinese government acquire strategically sensitive companies with chip technology. 2024年，美国政府将这家名为智路资本的私募股权公司列入商务部的“实体清单”，限制其与美国做生意。商务部称，智路资本曾协助中国政府收购拥有芯片技术的战略敏感企业。 Mr. Li is also the chairman of Tsinghua Unigroup, a technology conglomerate with government ownership. In 2021, one of Tsinghua Unigroup’s subsidiaries, New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, was added to the entity list for working with the Chinese military. 李斌同时还担任清华紫光集团董事长，这是一家国有的科技集团。2021年，清华紫光的一家子公司新华三半导体技术有限公司因与中国军方合作而被列入实体清单。 New Matrix is the second Chinese company approved to handle Nvidia’s H200 chips that does not seem to have any physical presence at its listed address. 新矩阵是第二家获准处理英伟达H200芯片、但其登记地址处似乎没有任何实体办公场所的中国公司。 今年9月，时报一名记者前往Maginfra的注册地址，那里看起来空无一人。 In September, The Times reported that another recently created Chinese firm called Maginfra had also received a license for H200s. Like New Matrix, Maginfra appears to have been approved not as the ultimate buyer of the chips, but as a company that would assemble them into A.I. servers for another customer. 《纽约时报》于9月报道称，另一家名为Maginfra的中国新成立公司也获得了H200芯片的出口许可。与New Matrix类似，Maginfra 获批的身份似乎并非这批芯片的最终买家，而是一家为其他客户将芯片组装进人工智能服务器的代工企业。 But when a Times reporter visited Maginfra’s listed address in China in September, it also appeared deserted. A few chairs and empty desks sat inside a small locked room with no signs. Workers on the floor said they had not seen anyone use the office, and building receptionists said they had not heard of Maginfra. 但时报记者9月前往Maginfra在中国的注册地址时，发现那里也空无一人。一间上了锁的小房间里摆放着几把椅子和几张空桌子，没有任何标识。该楼层的员工表示从未见过有人使用过这间办公室，大楼的前台接待人员则表示从未听说过Maginfra这家公司。 Analysts said they believed Maginfra was an offshoot of Inspur, a company whose headquarters were near Maginfra’s listed address. The U.S. government has added Inspur to the entity list for working with the Chinese military. Maginfra and Inspur share personnel and patents, and both have government ownership. 分析人士认为，Maginfra是浪潮集团(Inspur)的子公司，而浪潮集团的总部就在Maginfra的注册地址附近。美国政府已将浪潮集团列入实体清单，理由是其与中国军方有业务往来。Maginfra和浪潮集团共享人员和专利，且两家公司均有国资背景。 Military Ties 军方关系 Other Chinese companies that have been approved for licenses to buy Nvidia’s H200 chips also have ties through their corporate owners to military suppliers, according to people familiar with the approvals and documents viewed by The Times. 据熟悉审判情况的人士和《纽约时报》看到的文件，其他获准购买英伟达H200芯片许可证的中国公司也通过其公司所有者与军事供应商存在关联。 One, called Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology, has ties to a cloud computing giant that has sold services to military contractors, called Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group. Yindun is partly operated from a data center owned by Range, and several of its executives are family members of Range’s founder. 其中一家名为浙江银盾云科技的公司与云计算巨头润泽智算科技集团有关联，润泽智算曾向军事承包商出售服务。银盾部分业务在润泽拥有的数据中心运营，其几名高管是润泽创始人的家庭成员。 Range serves as the cloud computing provider for a satellite program run by the defense bureau of Hebei province, which it has described on its website as serving the strategic needs of “national defense development.” It also started a subsidiary in 2016 to focus on quantum communications for the Chinese government and military. Part of the subsidiary is owned by a firm that the United States added to the entity list in 2021 for acquiring American items for the Chinese military. 润泽是河北省国防部门运营的一个卫星项目的云计算提供商，该公司在其网站上称该项目服务于“国防发展”的战略需求。它还在2016年成立了一家子公司，专注于为中国政府和军方提供量子通信。该子公司部分股权由一家公司拥有，美国因该公司为中国军队采购美国物品，已于2021年将其列入实体清单。 Another company licensed to purchase H200 chips, Shanghai Jiatang, grew out of a state-owned enterprise called Datang Telecom, a chipmaker that provides technology to the Chinese military. Datang is controlled by the China Academy of Telecommunications Technology, a state-owned enterprise that has developed cryptography for the Chinese military. 另一家获准购买H200芯片的公司上海嘉唐源自一家名为大唐电信的国有企业。大唐电信是一家向中国军方提供技术的芯片制造商。大唐由中国电信科学技术研究院控制，这是一家为中国军方开发密码技术的国有企业。 Shanghai Jiatang, Yindun Cloud and Maginfra did not respond to requests for comment. 上海嘉唐、银盾云科技和Maginfra没有回应置评请求。 Ana Swanson报道贸易和国际经济新闻，常驻华盛顿。她从事新闻工作已超过十年。 Kalley Huang是时报驻旧金山记者，报道苹果公司和科技行业。 Keith Bradsher是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: ANA SWANSON, KALLEY HUANG, KEITH BRADSHER 2026年11月9日 北京的一处高科技企业工业园区。新矩阵公司将该建筑列为其地址，但园区公司名录中并未收录该企业。 The New York Times In a recently built industrial park on the northwest fringe of Beijing, the listed address of a company called New Matrix stands empty, a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be. 在北京西北郊一个最近建成的工业园区里，一家名为新矩阵的公司登记地址空无一人，那是一个空荡荡的灰色房间，天花板上本该装灯的地方垂着电线。 Earlier this year, the Trump administration approved this Chinese firm to assemble Nvidia’s advanced chips into the computers that create artificial intelligence. President Trump allowed the sale of the chips, called the H200, to China late last year. But before they could be sold, the Commerce Department was required to review the companies involved for national security risks. 今年早些时候，特朗普政府批准这家中国公司组装英伟达的先进芯片，用于创建人工智能的计算机。特朗普去年年底允许向中国出售这种名为H200的芯片。但在芯片出售之前，美国商务部必须对相关企业进行审查，以评估其是否存在国家安全风险。 New Matrix passed that review. Yet recent checks by The New York Times found that, within China, there is little evidence the firm actually exists, raising questions about who in China is behind the company. 新矩阵通过了这项审查。然而，《纽约时报》近期的核查发现，在中国国内，几乎没有证据表明这家公司真实存在，这引发了关于究竟是谁在幕后掌控这家公司的疑问。 Only scant information can be found online about New Matrix, which was created 17 months ago. At the building that New Matrix lists as its address, a company directory does not include the firm. At the nearby property management agency for the industrial park, a receptionist and a manager both said they had no record of the company. 关于这家17个月前成立的公司，网上只能找到极少信息。在新矩阵登记地址所在的大楼里，公司名录中没有这家公司。在附近工业园区的物业管理处，一名接待员和一名经理都说没有该公司的记录。 According to Chinese corporate records, New Matrix’s owners have ties to a prominent Chinese private equity fund that the U.S. government placed on a trade blacklist in 2024. Two analysts who examined the corporate records and other Chinese-language information said they believed New Matrix may be a front for firms associated with that fund. 根据中国企业登记记录，新矩阵的所有者与一家知名中国私募股权基金有关联，该基金已于2024年被美国政府列入贸易黑名单。两名审查了公司记录和其他中文信息的分析师表示，他们认为新矩阵可能是与该基金有关公司的幌子。 The sale of chips to New Matrix appears to be part of a pattern that has concerned technology experts inside and outside the government: The Commerce Department is giving clearance to buy and handle Nvidia’s chips to Chinese companies with ties to firms that have been subject to national-security-related trade restrictions. 芯片流向新矩阵似乎是令政府内外技术专家担忧的一种模式的一部分：美国商务部正在批准某些中国公司购买和处理英伟达芯片，而这些公司与此前被列入国家安全相关贸易限制的中国企业有关联。 Nvidia’s chips are the crucial technology in A.I. data centers and now one of the world’s most coveted commodities. They are also at the heart of the economic and geopolitical competition between the United States and China. 英伟达的芯片是人工智能数据中心的关键技术，如今也是世界上最抢手的商品之一。它们也是美中经济与地缘政治竞争的核心。 Corporate records show that several other Chinese companies approved to purchase H200 chips or assemble them into servers have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China. 公司记录显示，其他几家获准购买H200芯片或将其组装成服务器的中国公司与被美国政府列入黑名单的公司有关联，或者在中国担任军事承包商运营。 Liza Tobin, the former China director for the White House National Security Council in the first Trump and Biden administrations, said the approvals raised questions about how rigorously the Trump administration is policing who can get their hands on Nvidia’s chips. 曾在特朗普和拜登政府时期担任白宫国家安全委员会中国事务主任的莉莎·托宾说，这些批准引发了疑问：特朗普政府在监管谁能获得英伟达芯片方面究竟有多严格。 “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” she said. “我有很多担忧，商务部和英伟达都没有进行必要的尽职调查，以确保许可条款得到遵守，”她说。 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋，该公司的芯片是人工智能数据中心的关键技术，如今已成为全球最抢手的商品之一。 During the Biden administration, the United States began more broadly restricting sales of A.I. chips to China out of concern the technology would help China advance militarily. But Mr. Trump eased some of those limits after lobbying by Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, with whom he has grown close during his second term. 在拜登政府时期，美国开始更广泛地限制向中国出售人工智能芯片，担心该技术会帮助中国推进军事发展。但特朗普在英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的游说下放松了部分限制，他在第二任期内与黄仁勋的关系 日益密切 。 In December, Mr. Trump gave Nvidia permission to sell the H200, an older but still powerful A.I. chip, to China, as long as the U.S. government was given a cut of the sales. 去年12月，特朗普 允许英伟达 向中国出售H200——一款较旧但仍性能强大的人工智能芯片，条件是美国政府从销售中抽成。 In an unusual arrangement, Mr. Trump is requiring these chips, which are assembled in Taiwan, to be routed through the United States on their way to China, so that the government can collect a 25 percent tariff on their value. 在一项不同寻常的安排中，特朗普要求这些在台湾组装的芯片在运往中国途中经过美国，以便政府对其价值征收25%的关税。 Nvidia is now selling only small amounts of H200 chips to China. The Chinese government has been slow to approve its companies for the purchases, partly because it is trying to promote domestically made chips. 英伟达目前只向中国出售少量H200芯片。中国政府一直 缓慢批准 本国公司购买，部分原因是它试图推广国产芯片。 Although China is a potentially huge market for A.I. technology, sales directly to the country currently account for only a tiny percentage of Nvidia’s revenue. In the quarter that ended in July , H200 shipments to customers based in China made up less than 1 percent of Nvidia’s revenue from data centers. The company also said in August that it was not assuming any sales to China in its estimate for data center revenue for the current quarter. 尽管中国是人工智能技术的潜在巨大市场，但直接对华销售目前仅占英伟达收入的很小比例。 在截至7月的财季中 ，向位于中国的客户交付H200的出货量不到英伟达数据中心收入的1%。公司还在8月表示，在对本财季度数据中心营收的预估中，并未将对华销售额纳入考量。 But many Chinese companies are gaining access to Nvidia chips through data centers in Southeast Asia , and the chips still appear to be a critical focus for Beijing. The Times reported last month that Mr. Huang of Nvidia had a close relationship with a woman who American spy agencies concluded was an intelligence asset for China. The company she worked at, Megaspeed, operated data centers in Southeast Asia that served Chinese clients and was being investigated for smuggling some chips into China. On Sunday, Nvidia said that it was opening an investigation into Mr. Huang’s relationship with the woman after he acknowledged to the company’s board that he had been intimate with her. 但许多中国企业正通过 东南亚的数据中心 获得英伟达芯片，而这些芯片似乎仍是北京关注的焦点。《纽约时报》上个月报道，英伟达的黄仁勋与一名女性关系密切，美国间谍机构 认定她是中国的情报人员 。她所在的公司Megaspeed在东南亚运营数据中心，为中国客户服务，并因涉嫌将一些芯片走私到中国而受到调查。周日， 英伟达表示 ，在黄仁勋向公司董事会承认他与该女性有亲密关系后，公司正在调查黄仁勋与她的关系。 《纽约时报》记者走访时发现，获特朗普政府批准将英伟达的先进芯片组装成人工智能计算机的新矩阵公司登记地址处空无一人。 Another Empty Office 另一个空办公室 When the Commerce Department granted its approval to New Matrix this year, the company’s registered address was at a compound on the outskirts of Beijing used for corporate registrations, where thousands of other firms are also registered on paper, according to the Chinese corporate information site Qichacha. But two of its primary owners appear in the records of companies connected to a Chinese private equity firm under sanctions and its founder, a man named Li Bin, according to WireScreen, a data platform. 截至11月6日，新矩阵的网站没有列出任何员工姓名，没有布任何招聘信息，也没有包含关于其历史的信息。但根据数据平台WireScreen，其两名主要所有者出现在一家受制裁的中国私募股权公司及其创始人的关联企业记录中，该创始人名为李斌。 In 2024, the U.S. government added the private equity firm, Wise Road, to the Commerce Department’s “entity list,” which restricts companies from doing business with the United States. The department said Wise Road had helped the Chinese government acquire strategically sensitive companies with chip technology. 2024年，美国政府将这家名为智路资本的私募股权公司列入 商务部的“实体清单” ，限制其与美国做生意。商务部称，智路资本曾协助中国政府收购拥有芯片技术的战略敏感企业。 Mr. Li is also the chairman of Tsinghua Unigroup, a technology conglomerate with government ownership. In 2021, one of Tsinghua Unigroup’s subsidiaries, New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, was added to the entity list for working with the Chinese military. 李斌同时还担任清华紫光集团董事长，这是一家国有的科技集团。2021年，清华紫光的一家子公司新华三半导体技术有限公司因与中国军方合作而被列入 实体清单 。 New Matrix is the second Chinese company approved to handle Nvidia’s H200 chips that does not seem to have any physical presence at its listed address. 新矩阵是第二家获准处理英伟达H200芯片、但其登记地址处似乎没有任何实体办公场所的中国公司。 今年9月，时报一名记者前往Maginfra的注册地址，那里看起来空无一人。 In September, The Times reported that another recently created Chinese firm called Maginfra had also received a license for H200s. Like New Matrix, Maginfra appears to have been approved not as the ultimate buyer of the chips, but as a company that would assemble them into A.I. servers for another customer. 《纽约时报》于9月 报道 称，另一家名为Maginfra的中国新成立公司也获得了H200芯片的出口许可。与New Matrix类似，Maginfra 获批的身份似乎并非这批芯片的最终买家，而是一家为其他客户将芯片组装进人工智能服务器的代工企业。 But when a Times reporter visited Maginfra’s listed address in China in September, it also appeared deserted. A few chairs and empty desks sat inside a small locked room with no signs. Workers on the floor said they had not seen anyone use the office, and building receptionists said they had not heard of Maginfra. 但时报记者9月前往Maginfra在中国的注册地址时，发现那里也空无一人。一间上了锁的小房间里摆放着几把椅子和几张空桌子，没有任何标识。该楼层的员工表示从未见过有人使用过这间办公室，大楼的前台接待人员则表示从未听说过Maginfra这家公司。 Analysts said they believed Maginfra was an offshoot of Inspur, a company whose headquarters were near Maginfra’s listed address. The U.S. government has added Inspur to the entity list for working with the Chinese military. Maginfra and Inspur share personnel and patents, and both have government ownership. 分析人士认为，Maginfra是浪潮集团(Inspur)的子公司，而浪潮集团的总部就在Maginfra的注册地址附近。美国政府已将浪潮集团列入实体清单，理由是其与中国军方有业务往来。Maginfra和浪潮集团共享人员和专利，且两家公司均有国资背景。 Military Ties 军方关系 Other Chinese companies that have been approved for licenses to buy Nvidia’s H200 chips also have ties through their corporate owners to military suppliers, according to people familiar with the approvals and documents viewed by The Times. 据熟悉审判情况的人士和《纽约时报》看到的文件，其他获准购买英伟达H200芯片许可证的中国公司也通过其公司所有者与军事供应商存在关联。 One, called Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology, has ties to a cloud computing giant that has sold services to military contractors, called Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group. Yindun is partly operated from a data center owned by Range, and several of its executives are family members of Range’s founder. 其中一家名为浙江银盾云科技的公司与云计算巨头润泽智算科技集团有关联，润泽智算曾向军事承包商出售服务。银盾部分业务在润泽拥有的数据中心运营，其几名高管是润泽创始人的家庭成员。 Range serves as the cloud computing provider for a satellite program run by the defense bureau of Hebei province, which it has described on its website as serving the strategic needs of “national defense development.” It also started a subsidiary in 2016 to focus on quantum communications for the Chinese government and military. Datang is controlled by the China Academy of Telecommunications Technology, a state-owned enterprise that has developed cryptography for the Chinese military. 另一家获准购买H200芯片的公司上海嘉唐源自一家名为大唐电信的国有企业。大唐电信是一家向中国军方提供技术的芯片制造商。大唐由中国电信科学技术研究院控制，这是一家为中国军方开发密码技术的国有企业。 Shanghai Jiatang, Yindun Cloud and Maginfra did not respond to requests for comment. 上海嘉唐、银盾云科技和Maginfra没有回应置评请求。 Ana Swanson 报道贸易和国际经济新闻，常驻华盛顿。她从事新闻工作已超过十年。 Kalley Huang 是时报驻旧金山记者，报道苹果公司和科技行业。 Keith Bradsher 是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 接近黄仁勋的女间谍由中国国安部招募
description: JULIAN E. BARNES, TRIPP MICKLE, 孟建国, MAGGIE HABERMAN2026年11月9日英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋是特朗普总统颇具影响力的盟友，也是全球围绕人工智能主导地位的激烈竞争中的关键人物。 Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times A memo that circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring cited intelligence that a Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence. 据听取过相关情报简报的人士透露，今年春天，一份在特朗普政府高级决策官员之间传阅的备忘录援引情报称，一名与英伟达首席执行官关系密切的中国女商人是中国国家安全部的间谍。 The businesswoman, Alice Huang, was recruited to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, as part of a drive by Beijing’s top spy agency to learn more about American A.I. chips and potentially influence the company to push for its most advanced chips to be made available to China, the people said. 知情人士称，这名女商人叫黄乐(Alice Huang)，她被招募来搜集英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的情报。此举是中国最高情报机构的一项行动，目的是进一步了解美国的人工智能芯片，并谋求影响英伟达，促使该公司推动向中国出售其最先进的芯片。 Mr. Huang, an influential ally of President Trump’s, is a pivotal figure in the intense global competition for A.I. supremacy. Nvidia’s advanced chips are sought after around the world, and the company’s growth has helped drive the stock market over the past several years. 黄仁勋是特朗普总统有影响力的盟友，也是全球关于人工智能主导地位的激烈竞争的关键人物。英伟达的先进芯片在世界各地大受欢迎，公司的增长也成为过去几年推动股市上涨的重要力量。 The existence of the memo and the assessment by U.S. officials that Ms. Huang was working directly for the main Chinese intelligence agency have not previously been reported. They add important new detail to what appears to be an especially audacious example of China’s longstanding industrial espionage efforts. 这份备忘录的存在以及美国官员认定黄乐直接为中国主要情报机构工作的结论此前均未见报道。这些新披露的信息为中国长期以来从事工业间谍活动的一个尤为大胆的案例提供了重要的新细节。 China’s interest in Mr. Huang, and precisely what Beijing hoped to achieve by having one of its intelligence assets begin a close relationship with the executive, have been a focus of U.S. spy agencies. Those questions are now also of interest to Capitol Hill. On Thursday, the Republican leaders of three influential House committees requested that Mr. Huang appear before them later this month in a closed-door briefing regarding his interactions with Ms. Huang, who is not related. 中国为何对黄仁勋感兴趣、北京希望通过让一名情报人员与他建立密切关系达到什么目的一直是美国情报机构关注的重点。这些问题现在也引起了国会的兴趣。周四，众议院三个重要委员会的共和党领导人要求黄仁勋在本月晚些时候出席一场闭门简报会，就他与黄乐的往来情况给出说明。 2024年6月，黄仁勋与Megaspeed高管黄乐及其他科技企业高管在台北参加一场行业聚会。照片由NetThunder公司发布在领英上。 The New York Times reported last week that Mr. Huang was a target of a Chinese intelligence operation, and that U.S. intelligence agencies were conducting electronic surveillance of Ms. Huang, a Chinese citizen, for at least a year. The Times reported that Mr. Trump had been briefed last year about Mr. Huang’s relationship with her, but chose not to do anything about it. 《纽约时报》上周报道，黄仁勋是中国一项情报行动的目标，美国情报机构已对身为中国公民的黄乐实施了至少一年的电子监控。《纽约时报》还报道，特朗普去年曾听取有关黄仁勋与黄乐关系的简报，但决定不采取任何行动。 Ms. Huang speaks English well and has relationships with executives at the highest levels of the A.I. chip industry, including Mr. Huang and the leaders of Gigabyte, one of the top assemblers of Nvidia supercomputers, said people who have met her. She has attended industry conferences and private executive dinners. 见过黄乐的人说，她英语流利，与人工智能芯片行业的最高层保持着联系，包括黄仁勋和技嘉科技(Gigabyte)的领导人，技嘉科技是英伟达超级计算机的主要组装商之一。黄乐曾出席行业会议和高管私人晚宴。 It is unclear when Ms. Huang first met Nvidia’s leader. In 2024, around the time the two of them were photographed together at a bar in Taipei, her company, Megaspeed, began a multibillion-dollar purchase of advanced A.I. microchips. 目前不清楚黄乐第一次见到英伟达领导人是什么时候。2024年，两人在台北一家酒吧合影前后，她的公司Megaspeed开始采购价值数十亿美元的先进人工智能微芯片。 To many in the industry, the well-funded push by Megaspeed into A.I. appeared to come out of nowhere. 在许多业内人士看来，Megaspeed手握雄厚资金突然大举进军人工智能领域令人颇感意外。 Ms. Huang was connected to a network of companies and investors clustered around Shanghai and Zhejiang province that had used their ties to local officials in Shanghai to push aggressively from mobile video games into data centers, which provide the computing power behind artificial intelligence. 黄乐与一个集中在上海和浙江省的企业及投资者网络存在联系。这个网络利用与上海地方官员的关系，积极推动业务从手机游戏向数据中心扩张。数据中心提供人工智能运行所需的算力。 Megaspeed has been building data centers in Southeast Asia and then renting their computing power to Alibaba, the giant Chinese internet firm, giving China a backdoor way of getting access to advanced Nvidia chips. Nvidia is restricted by the United States from selling those chips directly to China. Megaspeed一直在东南亚建设数据中心，然后将算力出租给中国互联网巨头阿里巴巴，使中国得以通过一条间接渠道使用英伟达的先进芯片。美国限制英伟达直接向中国销售这些芯片。 Beyond its local connections, the network also has a financial link to the Chinese military establishment, through an investment in a cybersecurity subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group, one of the country’s largest makers of military technology. 除了地方关系，这个企业网络还通过投资中国电子科技集团旗下的一家网络安全子公司与中国军工体系存在财务联系。中国电子科技集团是中国最大的军事技术制造商之一。 去年在华盛顿举行的一场英伟达大会展览活动上，人们参观计算技术展示。 The Chinese government has set goals to overtake the United States as the world’s leader in A.I. technology by 2030. The focus on A.I. has increased across the parts of the Chinese government that specialize in national security, including the spy agency that recruited Ms. Huang. 中国政府已制定目标，要在2030年前超越美国，成为全球人工智能技术的领导者。中国政府内部负责国家安全的部门日益重视人工智能，其中就包括招募黄乐的情报机构。 China’s M.S.S. spy agency was once a backwater. But when Xi Jinping took over as China’s leader in 2012, he began to invest in the agency. Today it is many times larger than the C.I.A., collecting human intelligence and intercepting electronic communications. The agency also conducts counterintelligence operations. 中国国家安全部曾经是一个不起眼的边缘部门。但习近平2012年成为中国领导人后开始加大对该机构的投入。如今，国安部的规模已是美国中央情报局的数倍，既搜集人力情报，也截获电子通信信息，同时还开展反间谍行动。 Peter Mattis, a former C.I.A. counterintelligence analyst, said China’s spy agency had made technology a focus of its activities, seeing it as “the key fight for dominance in the economic world.” 曾任美国中央情报局反间谍分析师的彼得·马蒂斯表示，中国的情报机构已将技术列为工作重点，认为技术是“争夺全球经济主导地位的关键战场”。 “They’re interested in what’s taking place in technology, in the technical specifications of what’s being built and in shaping decision-making as it relates to those things,” said Mr. Mattis, who is now the president of the Jamestown Foundation, a national security think tank. “Jensen is someone you’d want to influence because he wields a lot of power and is at the crux of a world-shaping technology.” “他们关注科技领域正在发生的变化、正在开发的技术有哪些具体规格，以及如何影响与这些技术相关的决策，”现任国家安全智库詹姆斯敦基金会主席的马蒂斯说。“黄仁勋正是他们希望施加影响的人，因为他拥有巨大的影响力，而且身处一项足以改变世界的技术的关键位置。” John Rizzo, an Nvidia spokesman, said that the company does not share classified information with its customers, and that customers do not ask Nvidia to press the U.S. government to change its policies on chip sales to China. 英伟达发言人约翰·里佐表示，公司不会与客户分享机密信息，客户也不会要求英伟达向美国政府施压，改变对华芯片销售政策。 He added that the Chinese government had “consistently promoted its own domestic alternatives in China, including Huawei, and strictly limited imports of our data center products.” 他还说，中国政府“一直在中国推广包括华为在内的本土替代产品，并严格限制进口我们的数据中心产品”。 Mr. Rizzo has maintained that Mr. Huang’s interactions with Ms. Huang were “not unusual” and consistent with the kinds of meetings he has with any of Nvidia’s many customers. 里佐一直坚称，黄仁勋与黄乐的往来“并无异常”，与他同英伟达众多客户举行的其他会面没有区别。 Liu Chang, a spokesman for the Chinese embassy, said The Times reporting was “unsubstantiated” and “nothing but smears against China.” Ms. Huang has not responded to multiple attempts to reach her for comment in recent days. Mr. Rizzo previously said that Mr. Huang’s interactions with Ms. Huang were “not unusual,” and that he speaks annually with thousands of executives who do business with Nvidia. 中国驻美国大使馆发言人刘畅表示，《纽约时报》的报道“毫无根据”，“纯属对中国的污蔑”。记者近日多次尝试联系黄乐请其置评，但均未得到回应。里佐此前表示，黄仁勋与黄乐的往来“并无异常”，而且黄仁勋每年都会与数千名同英伟达有业务往来的高管交谈。 Spokeswomen for the White House and C.I.A. declined to comment. 白宫和中央情报局的发言人均拒绝置评。 Mr. Huang has been steadfast over the past several years in calling for the U.S. government to permit chip makers to sell A.I. technology to China. He has argued that doing so would create competition for Huawei, China’s tech giant, and slow its development of A.I. technology. 过去几年里，黄仁勋始终坚定主张美国政府应允许芯片制造商向中国销售人工智能技术。他认为，这样做可以为中国科技巨头华为制造竞争，从而减缓其人工智能技术的发展。 今年9月，黄仁勋与特朗普总统在白宫出席一场人工智能主题午宴。 In 2025, he persuaded Mr. Trump to roll back a prohibition on A.I. chip sales to China and allow Nvidia to sell a less powerful chip there. He and the president later struck a deal to sell the company’s second-most-powerful chip to China, with the United States taking a 25 percent cut of sales. Mr. Trump later considered allowing Nvidia to sell China its latest chip, known as Blackwell. But he has backed off that idea. 2025年，他说服特朗普撤销对华销售人工智能芯片的禁令，允许英伟达向中国出售一款性能较低的芯片。后来，他又与特朗普达成协议，允许公司向中国销售其性能第二强的芯片，美国政府则从销售额中抽取25%。此后，特朗普还考虑过允许英伟达向中国出售其最新的Blackwell芯片，但最终放弃了这一想法。 Speaking at an investor conference in May, Mr. Huang said that China should not have access to Nvidia’s best technology, like its Blackwell chips or its forthcoming Rubin chip. He said the United States should have “the first, the most and the best, but simultaneously all American companies should compete globally.” 今年5月，黄仁勋在一场投资者会议上表示，中国不应获得英伟达最先进的技术，例如Blackwell芯片或即将推出的Rubin芯片。他说，美国应该“最先拿到、拿到最多、拿到最好的技术，但与此同时，所有美国公司都应该参与全球竞争”。 Founded in 1983, China’s M.S.S. spy agency long failed to win the confidence of the country’s leaders. The espionage and cyber-hacking arms of the People’s Liberation Army were for years considered the primary intelligence collection arms of Beijing. 中国国家安全部成立于1983年，一直以来未能赢得国家领导层的信任。多年来，中国人民解放军的间谍和网络黑客部门一直被视为北京主要的情报搜集力量。 The agency took on more of China’s espionage work after Beijing and Washington struck a deal in 2015 to curb cyberoperations, according to researchers and U.S. officials. In the years that followed, the Justice Department accused hackers associated with the M.S.S. of attempting to steal U.S. technology and infiltrate U.S. networks. 据研究人员和美国官员称，2015年北京与华盛顿达成限制网络行动的协议后，国家安全部承担了更多中国的间谍活动。此后数年，美国司法部指控与国家安全部有关联的黑客试图窃取美国技术，并渗透美国的网络。 By 2023, the agency had emerged as a rival to the C.I.A., and began using A.I. to select and profile targets. It had expanded its network of spies through aggressive recruitment, and used its bigger budget to help Mr. Xi in his ambitions to challenge U.S. dominance. 到2023年，国家安全部已发展成为美国中央情报局的竞争对手，并开始利用人工智能筛选情报目标、建立目标画像。该机构通过大规模招募扩大了间谍网络，还利用增加的预算，协助习近平实现挑战美国主导地位的雄心。 The M.S.S. also used its ties to various Chinese companies to expand its work, in cyber-hacking, espionage and information operations. It is estimated to have hundreds of thousands of agents, which dwarfs the number of counterintelligence officers in the United States. 国家安全部还利用与多家中国公司的关系来扩展其在网络黑客、间谍活动和信息行动方面的工作。据估计，该机构拥有数十万名特工，远远超过美国反间谍人员的数量。 The agency continues to largely operate behind the scenes, but under its current leader, Chen Yixin, it has also taken on a more public role in Chinese life. In 2023, the agency created a WeChat account, mainly for domestic propaganda and for encouraging Chinese citizens to report people suspected of being foreign spies. The channel is also used to attack the United States for a supposed Cold War mind-set. 国家安全部在很大程度上仍继续在幕后运作，但在现任部长陈一新的领导下，它在中国社会生活中也扮演了更加公开的角色。2023年，该机构开设了一个微信公众号，主要用于国内宣传，并鼓励中国公民举报疑似外国间谍的人员。该公众号还被用来攻击美国，称其抱有所谓的冷战思维。 Mr. Chen is very familiar with the region of eastern China where Ms. Huang operates. A Zhejiang native, he spent a major part of his long career working for the province’s Chinese Communist Party. He served under Mr. Xi when Mr. Xi ran Zhejiang in the early 2000s. Political analysts say their ties are close. 陈一新非常熟悉黄乐从事商业活动的华东地区。他是浙江人，在漫长的职业生涯中，大部分时间都在为该省的中共党组织工作。习近平在2000年代初主政浙江期间，陈一新曾在其手下任职。政治分析人士称两人关系密切。 Mr. Chen has been outspoken about the risks A.I. poses to the Chinese Communist Party. In a September essay in the state-run magazine China Cyberspace, he said that China needed to assert control over A.I. to protect political stability at home, defend against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks and compete militarily with the United States. He said algorithms would help countries “gain the initiative on the battlefield.” 陈一新一直直言不讳地谈论人工智能对中国共产党构成的风险。在9月发表于官方杂志《中国网信》的一篇文章中，他说中国需要加强对人工智能的控制，以维护国内政治稳定、防范日益复杂的网络攻击，并在军事领域与美国竞争。他表示，算法将帮助各国“赢得战场主动权”。 Julian E. Barnes为《纽约时报》报道美国情报机构和国际安全事务。他撰写安全相关议题已有20余年。 Tripp Mickle报道英伟达、谷歌和苹果等全球最大的科技公司。他也报道整个科技行业的趋势，包括裁员、生成式AI和机器人出租车等。 Maggie Haberman是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统。 孟建国(Paul Mozur)是时报全球科技记者，常驻台北。此前，他自香港、上海和首尔报道亚洲科技与政治的交叉议题。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
